title: Who's Who: Nadia al-Khatib
summary: Surveyor of layers whose work remains part of the record of modern Eidetics.
author: Who's Who Desk
paragraphs: The Correspondent adds Nadia al-Khatib (1818–1880) to its Who's Who of Eideticians, recording a surveyor of layers whose name still attends serious discussion of the Eidetic Stratum.

Al-Khatib replaced familiar compass directions with a layered itinerary keyed to the Prime Referent and sonance offset. Her 1851 reckoning let teams compare journeys through regions where apparent distance had little meaning.
She reserved blank space in every chart for the possibility that a mapped route might drift.

For Alderwick readers, Nadia al-Khatib is remembered not as an ornament to legend but as a figure whose work helps explain why Eideticians prize careful terms, repeatable evidence and a sober account of what remains unknown.
